title: Zelenskyy Warns of Major New Russian Strike as Trump Urges Putin to Pull Back
excerpt: Ukraine says Russia is completing preparations for a massive strike on its energy grid. Trump says he pressed Putin in China to end military aggression across Europe, while his envoys describe the peace talks as deadlocked over territory.
body:
• President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on Thursday that Russia is completing preparations for a new massive strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, and urged people to heed air-raid alarms in the coming days.
  • US President Donald Trump said he had urged Vladimir Putin to "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe" so a deal between Russia and Ukraine can be "made quickly."
  • US envoy Jared Kushner, who is mediating talks with Steve Witkoff, said Putin has "shown restraint" by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons, but that the talks are at "a little bit of a deadlock" over Ukrainian territory.
  • Overnight Russian strikes with ballistic missiles and 113 drones hit 20 locations; crews are restoring power in six regions.

Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Thursday, warning citizens to pay attention to missile-threat alarms in the coming days.

"Unfortunately, we have information about a new mass strike being prepared by the Russians," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address, according to Al Jazeera. "In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats." It was his second such warning this week. Ukrainian intelligence indicates Moscow is "completing preparations for a new massive strike," he said on social media, adding: "We will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike."

The grid under attack, again

Russian missile and drone attacks have battered Ukraine's power grid since the invasion, in what Kyiv says is an effort to deprive civilians of light, heating and running water as winter approaches. "The Russians continue to target substations, overhead power lines, and the entire power grid," Zelenskyy said. Crews are working to restore electricity in six regions after Russia launched ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight; Ukraine's air force reported hits at 20 locations, striking an apartment building and damaging a hospital, a sports facility, businesses and a gas station, officials said. In Kyiv, ballistic missiles wounded seven people and hit a shopping centre and two other buildings, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. On November 20, Russia fired more than 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine, killing eight people, Zelenskyy said. Ukraine is pressing partners for more air-defence supplies, especially interceptors for US-made Patriot systems, which have been in short supply.

"Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH."

— Donald Trump, US President, on Truth Social

Trump urges Putin to pull back

US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease Russia's military actions in Europe. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he spent "a lot of time" in talks with Putin in China on Putin pulling back "all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," and that he hoped this would allow a deal between Russia and Ukraine to be "made quickly," which he called "a strong possibility." Trump said he updated NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte on the talks during a meeting at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Wednesday night, and in another post said Ukrainian and Russian forces alike should avoid "any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the War."

Envoys, and the other side

Jared Kushner, who is mediating Russia-Ukraine talks with envoy Steve Witkoff, said after talking at length with Putin that he believes the Russian leader wants peace, almost five years after Moscow invaded Ukraine. Putin "has agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention," Kushner said on the MD Meets podcast, adding that "what (Putin) is saying is peace, but I think it's always peace on what terms," with the talks at "a little bit of a deadlock" over the fate of Ukrainian territory. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Thursday that the United States is approaching the talks with an understanding of the need to eliminate what Russia calls the "root causes" of the conflict, including "the creation of threats to Russia's security right on our borders."

Signs the war is widening

Ukraine has used domestically produced long-range weapons against targets in Russia and struck a Russian naval vessel docked at a port in Libya with sea drones last weekend — an expansion that alarmed some European leaders. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said Thursday she supported Ukraine's fight but that the war "should not and cannot be expanded to the Mediterranean." Ukrainian forces also struck a Russian military airfield and an oil pumping facility overnight, Ukraine's General Staff said, while the Russian Defense Ministry said its forces intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones overnight. For now, the diplomacy and the preparations are moving in opposite directions: envoys describe a deadlock over territory, and Kyiv is bracing for the next mass strike.
